summary.headline: Castrol India Q1 FY26 revenue rose 9% to INR1,545 crore and EBITDA 7% to INR329 crore, with management flagging raw-material cost pressure from Q2.
summary.overview: Castrol India reported Q1 FY26 revenue of INR1,545 crore (up 9%), EBITDA of INR329 crore (up 7%) and PAT of INR242 crore (up 4%), with volume growth of 7-8% YoY. Management said the Middle East conflict and weaker rupee (about 6.5-7% down YoY) began to hit costs late in the quarter, but minimal raw-material inflation reached Q1 COGS because of inventory cycles. One round of price increases was taken at end-March, and the bulk of raw-material cost increases is expected in Q2. Operating expenses rose sharply QoQ, which management attributed partly to one-time employee costs expected to fall in coming quarters.

financial_highlights.change: about +10% YoY and about +23% QoQ (analyst figure, not disputed)

segments.name: Rural
segments.commentary: Volume growing at double-digit rate for several years; distribution expanded to about 40,000 outlets, 700 Rural Service Express bike units added, and direct reach into villages below 20,000 population. About two-thirds of rural product sales are motorcycle products.

segments.name: Urban premium (cars and bikes)
segments.commentary: Premium brands delivered double-digit volume and value growth in the quarter; cars are an emerging segment, estimated at 15-20% of revenue.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Management says CV has been strong and the Tata Motors partnership grew in double digits, but the wider CV and specialty range (truck engine oil, transmission fluids, greases) grew only high single-digit. Automotive two-wheeler plus CV together is about 60% of sales.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Growing at double-digit for multiple consecutive quarters; weighted-average margin is lower than automotive, though some niche applications are high margin.

segments.name: Service network
segments.commentary: 800 Castrol Auto Services at end-March; 34,000 independent bike workshops and 13,000 multi-brand car workshops reached.

guidance_outlook: Structural EBITDA margin band of 21-24% retained as the target; management said Q1 is seasonally the softest quarter and Q1 margin dilution was not large.
Raw-material cost increases (crude, packaging, fuel, additives) expected to flow into COGS from Q2 FY26; one round of pricing taken end-March, with further price-plus-cost-cut actions possible.
One-time employee costs in Q1 opex are expected to decline, so future quarterly opex should be lower than Q1 levels.
Parent-level deal remains subject to global regulatory approvals; management says there is no change to Castrol India's structure, strategy or operating model.
No guidance given on data-centre cooling opportunity.
capex_capacity: No capacity, capex or utilisation figures were discussed on the call.
Base oil sourced from Indian refiners, Singapore and South Korea; imports driven by specification needs, and the company is open to other sources.
Term base-oil contracts are index-linked (Argus and ICIS); no scarcity premium reported as of call date.
MoU signed with Hindustan Petroleum Corporation to explore a re-refined base oil ecosystem in India.
Data-centre cooling (immersion and direct-to-chip) is at trial stage in India; no timeline or market size given.
demand_pricing: Hedging: 60-day policy linked to inventory cycle; about half of COGS is locally sourced (not hedged) and half imported (USD exposure hedged).
Pricing: no blanket increase; price changes set product by product to recover cost increases, with intent to hold margins.
Rural margins described as accretive, with premium bike oils (Activ) carrying high gross margins; car margins highest, then bikes, then CVs.
Competition in EV space: partnerships with Ather Energy (2W) and Tata Mobility (EV transmission fluids), with products for hybrid, E20 and gas engines already in market.
Middle East sourcing pressure: higher cost and less predictable lead times for feedstocks; no material supply disruption yet.

qa_highlights.question: Has the crude price spike in March flowed into Q1 raw-material costs, and how fast can price increases pass through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said minimal raw-material impact hit Q1 COGS due to inventory cycles, with the main impact being FX; most cost increases are expected in Q2. One round of pricing was taken at end-March.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating expenses rise about 23% QoQ and 10% YoY, and what is the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total expenses grew 9%, in line with revenue, and COGS grew slower than volume. Some one-time employee costs sit in the quarter and should fall, so future quarters should be lower than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7-8% volume growth YoY or QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is Q1 FY26 versus Q1 FY25, YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin should be expected for the year, given the drop to about 21%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the 21-24% operating EBITDA band. Q1 is seasonally soft and not heavily diluted, but short-term volatility could come as raw-material costs rise.

qa_highlights.question: Are base-oil prices showing a premium or scarcity pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts are index-linked to Argus and ICIS, which have moved up. No separate scarcity premium is applied to term contracts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data-centre opportunity, its timeline and its market size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the work is beyond pilot, with trials under way in India, but gave no timeline, guidance or market size because technology choices are not yet firm.

qa_highlights.question: Which segment is pulling down overall volume growth despite double-digit growth in rural and premium urban?
qa_highlights.answer: Large commercial vehicle business, including truck engine oil, plus specialty products such as transmission fluids and greases, grew high single-digit, which pulls the blended rate to 7-8%.

risks_watch: Raw-material and feedstock cost inflation (crude, packaging, additives) and FX pressure from Q2 FY26, with only one price increase taken so far.
Margin band: whether EBITDA stays within 21-24% as the pricing and cost-cut response plays out.
Sustainability of opex: confirm that one-time employee costs decline in Q2 and beyond.
Middle East sourcing: lead-time unpredictability and possible supply gaps despite diversified sourcing.
Parent-level transaction: regulatory approvals pending; management says no operating change at Castrol India.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Q1 execution and earnings quality, but noticeably cautious on the outlook: management repeatedly flagged near-term volatility and cost pressure from Q2. Answers on pricing quantum, the one-time cost amount and data-centre timelines were evasive or non-quantified.
key_quotes: We have delivered our 12th consecutive quarter of stable revenue and volume growth.
Given the inventory cycle, we saw minimal impact of these raw material increases into the COGS that we reported in quarter 1.
Structurally, we will recover the structural margin for the company, we will want to go back into that same range of 21%, 24%.
So, we don't see rural as a gross margin dilutor for us at all.

growth.why: Q1 revenue +9% and EBITDA +7% YoY with 7-8% volume growth, but no revenue growth guidance was given; the 21-24% structural EBITDA margin band is reiterated while raw-material cost inflation is expected from Q2 and only one price round has been taken, so outlook is flat to unclear with no capacity, capex or utilisation data.
